name: @pipeworx/mcp-patents

tools.name: search_patents
tools.description: Search USPTO patent applications and grants — **without a `granted_after`/`granted_before` bound this returns the APPLICATION corpus sorted newest-FILED-first, not issued patents.** USPTO publishes an application ~18 months after filing and typically takes 2+ years to grant it, so the newest rows in an unfiltered search are always recent, unexamined filings with `grant_date: null` — that is expected, not stale data. **Pick the date field on the QUESTION'S VERB, not on the word "recent":** a question asking who has FILED / applied for / sought patents in a window wants `filed_after`/`filed_before` — the default application corpus already includes pending AND granted patents, so no `granted_after` is needed or wanted, and adding one will silently drop recently-filed-but-not-yet-examined applications (grant lags filing by 2+ years, so "filed in the last 3 years" AND "granted in the last 3 years" are mostly DISJOINT sets). Only use `granted_after`/`granted_before` when the question explicitly says GRANTED / ISSUED / APPROVED / "has a patent" (not just "recent patents"). Use `query` for free-text keywords ("lithium battery", "crispr", "machine learning"); all terms are required (AND), and you can quote a phrase to keep it together. A curated, short list of known synonym/abbreviation pairs for concepts that patents describe inconsistently (e.g. cfRNA / cell-free RNA / circulating RNA; MRD / minimal residual disease / residual cancer) is recognized in `query` — quoted or bare — and expanded to an OR group before the search runs, so "cfRNA" and "cell-free RNA" are treated as the same concept rather than requiring the caller to guess a specific patent's exact wording (marked `synonyms_expanded: true` in the response; this is a fixed, documented list, not general synonym invention). A question that names several DISTINCT ways of describing the same idea (e.g. a condition plus a detection method, each expressed as its own quoted phrase) should still be passed as one query — if the literal AND-of-everything match returns zero, the tool automatically retries once with those same quoted phrases OR'd together instead and marks the response `broadened: true`; it only ever relaxes multi-phrase AND to OR on a genuine zero, so a search that is narrow for a real reason (e.g. one specific applicant with no matching filings, or an ordinary bare-keyword AND) still correctly returns zero. Optional structured filters: `applicant` (exact corporate name as filed, e.g. "APPLE INC."), `inventor` (person name), `title` (words in the invention title), `number` (a specific application number), `filed_after` / `filed_before`, `granted_after` / `granted_before`. Common synonyms are understood — `assignee`, `company` and `owner` all reach `applicant`, and `keywords`, `q` or `text` all reach `query`. Results include title, application number, filing date, first applicant, all applicants, inventors, status, classification. `total` is the full match count but USPTO returns at most 25 records per search — narrow with applicant or a date range rather than raising `limit`. Powered by the USPTO Open Data Portal (data.uspto.gov).

query.description: Free-text keywords. Every term must appear (they are AND-ed), so add words to narrow and remove words to widen. Wrap words in double quotes to require them adjacent: `"machine learning" model` needs the exact phrase plus the word model. Examples: "lithium battery", "crispr", "neural network". Pass "*" if you only want to filter by applicant/date with no keyword constraint. A curated set of known synonyms/abbreviations (e.g. cfRNA / cell-free RNA / circulating RNA, or MRD / minimal residual disease / residual cancer) is automatically expanded to an OR group within the query — quoted or bare, either form is recognized — so you do not need to guess which exact wording a given patent uses (see `synonyms_expanded` in the response). If several quoted phrases — or two recognized synonym-group concepts, quoted or not — ANDed together still match nothing, the tool retries once with them OR'd instead (see `broadened` in the response) rather than returning a bare zero.

applicant.description: Optional. Company applicant name as it appears on the USPTO filing. This is also how to list the patents a company OWNS or holds ("patents assigned to X", "X's patents", "patents owned by X"): set `applicant`, with `query` "*" if there is no keyword. **Must include the exact corporate suffix** the company uses (PBC / Inc. / LLC / Corporation / Co. / NV / AG / KK). A wrong or missing suffix matches nothing — "Apple" returns zero where "APPLE INC." returns hundreds. Examples: "Anthropic, PBC" (not "Anthropic Inc."), "Apple Inc." (not "Apple"), "Alphabet Inc." (not "Google"), "Meta Platforms, Inc." (not "Facebook"), "Microsoft Corporation" (not "Microsoft Corp."). If you get zero results plus a `warning` field, the name form is wrong rather than the company being absent — retry with a different corporate form.

inventor.description: Optional. Inventor name as recorded on the filing; a last name matches most reliably. Examples: "Hinton", "Bengio". Accepted synonyms: `inventor_name`, `author`.

title.description: Optional. Words that must appear in the invention title, which narrows far harder than `query` does since `query` searches the whole record. Example: "solid state battery".

number.description: Optional. A specific US application number, digits only or formatted — "16123456" or "16/123,456". Accepted synonyms: `application_number`, `patent_number`.

filed_after.description: Optional. Filter to patents FILED on/after this date (ISO YYYY-MM-DD). Use this for "who has filed / applied for patents on X (recently / in the last N years)" — it covers both pending applications and already-granted patents, so it is the right bound even when the question also says "recent". Do NOT substitute `granted_after` for a filing-activity question: grant lags filing by 2+ years, so a recent filing window under `granted_after` typically returns zero even when filing activity is real.

filed_before.description: Optional. Filter to patents FILED on/before this date (ISO YYYY-MM-DD).

granted_after.description: Optional. Filter to patents GRANTED (issued) on/after this date (ISO YYYY-MM-DD) — use ONLY when the question explicitly says GRANTED / ISSUED / APPROVED, not for a plain "recent patents" or "who has filed" question (use `filed_after` for those — see its description). Accepted synonym: `issued_after`.

granted_before.description: Optional. Filter to patents GRANTED (issued) on/before this date (ISO YYYY-MM-DD). Accepted synonym: `issued_before`.

limit.description: Number of results to return (default 10). USPTO caps every search at 25 records, so values above 25 have no effect — use the filters to narrow instead.

_apiKey.description: USPTO ODP API key. Get free at https://data.uspto.gov/myodp. Falls back to platform key if configured.

tools.name: get_patent
tools.description: Fetch a single USPTO patent application/grant by application number (`number`, e.g. "16/123,456" or "16123456") or by an already-granted patent number (`patent_number`, e.g. "11646472") — pass whichever one you actually have. Returns full metadata: title, inventors, classifications, status, and — when the application has been granted — `patent_number`, `grant_date`, `publication_number`, `publication_date`. **8-digit application numbers and 8-digit patent numbers can be the SAME digit string for a different record** (application series codes 10-12 were used ~2003-2008, and granted patent numbers entered that same 10,000,000-12,999,999 range in 2018 and are still in it) — e.g. "11646472" is BOTH application 11/646,472 (a 2006 filing) AND patent 11,646,472 (a 2023 grant), two unrelated inventions. If you only pass `number` and it is an 8-digit value in that collision range, this tool checks BOTH interpretations; if both exist, it returns `ambiguous: true` with each record summarized rather than silently guessing — re-call with `number` for the application or `patent_number` for the patent. Passing `patent_number` explicitly always skips the ambiguity check. A `status` of "Patented Case" with `patent_number: null` means USPTO ODP omitted that field for this record (check `patent_number_warning`), not that the patent was never granted; a pending application correctly has `patent_number: null`, `grant_date: null`.

number.description: An application number, digits only or with slashes (e.g. "16123456", "16/123,456"). If this happens to also be a valid 8-digit granted patent number (see the collision note above), the response may come back `ambiguous: true` — pass `patent_number` instead to mean the patent unambiguously.

patent_number.description: An already-granted US patent number, digits only (e.g. "11646472", "10000000"). Use this instead of `number` whenever you specifically mean the patent, not the application — it is never ambiguous.

_apiKey.description: USPTO ODP API key. Get free at https://data.uspto.gov/myodp.

tools.name: search_inventors
tools.description: Search USPTO patent applications by inventor last name. Returns matching applications with title, inventor list, and filing date — sorted newest-filed-first, so this is the APPLICATION corpus (same as search_patents with no `granted_after`), and the newest rows will be unexamined filings with no grant date by construction (USPTO publishes ~18 months after filing). That is expected, not stale data. For a specific inventor's ISSUED patents, use search_patents with `inventor` + `granted_after` instead.

query.description: Inventor last name to search for (case-insensitive). Examples: "Hinton", "Bengio".

limit.description: Number of results to return (default 10). USPTO caps every search at 25 records, so values above 25 have no effect — use the filters to narrow instead.

_apiKey.description: USPTO ODP API key. Get free at https://data.uspto.gov/myodp.

tools.name: get_patent_assignments
tools.description: Retrieve USPTO-recorded assignment/conveyance history for one patent application from the migrated Open Data Portal endpoint. Returns assignors, assignees, execution/recording dates, conveyance text, and reel/frame. A recorded assignment is notice of a submitted instrument—not a legal opinion on present title, validity, scope, liens, or chain-of-title completeness.

application_number.description: US patent application number, digits only or formatted, e.g. "15/000,001".

_apiKey.description: USPTO ODP API key. Get free at https://data.uspto.gov/myodp.

tools.name: get_patent_transactions
tools.description: Fetch the full USPTO prosecution/transaction history for one patent application — every dated event the Office recorded against the case (filings, mailings, fee payments, office actions, notices, the grant itself), newest first. This is a superset of the handful of events `get_patent` surfaces: use this tool when the question is about the PROSECUTION HISTORY itself (how many office actions, when was it mailed, when did examination start) rather than just the current status.

number.description: US application number, digits only or formatted. Examples: "18926509", "16/123,456".

limit.description: Maximum number of events to return, newest first (default 50). The full history is usually under 100 events; a `note` in the response says when more exist than were returned.

_apiKey.description: USPTO ODP API key. Get free at https://data.uspto.gov/myodp.

tools.name: get_patent_continuity
tools.description: Fetch the parent/child continuity (priority) chain for one patent application — every earlier application this one claims priority from (continuation, divisional, CIP, provisional, etc.) and every later application that in turn claims priority from it, each with the claim type, dates, and the parent/child's own patent number where granted. Use this to answer "what did this patent come from" or "what later patents/applications descend from this one". An application with no continuity relationships returns an empty chain on both sides — that is a real, common answer (most applications are standalone filings), not a failure.

number.description: US application number, digits only or formatted. Examples: "17248024", "16/123,456".

_apiKey.description: USPTO ODP API key. Get free at https://data.uspto.gov/myodp.

tools.name: search_patent_assignments
tools.description: Search USPTO-recorded patent assignment/conveyance history by assignee, assignor, a granted patent number, or an application number — one of the four is required. Unlike `get_patent_assignments` (which needs an application number you already have), this answers "what has company X been assigned" or "who assigned patent Y". An `assignee`/`assignor` search returns one row per recorded assignment (reel/frame, conveyance, dates, the other party) and additionally resolves the covered property (application/patent number, title) for each one it returns via a follow-up lookup — capped by `limit` because each one is a separate upstream call. A `patent_number`/`application_number` search returns the full assignment chain for that one property directly. An assignee/assignor with no recorded assignments returns a plain zero with the upstream total, not an error — USPTO assignment coverage is uneven for older or never-assigned properties. Individual (non-corporate) assignee addresses are omitted; company addresses are kept. Powered by the USPTO Assignment Search system (public, no account or key required).

assignee.description: Company or person that RECEIVED rights in a recorded transfer (the recipient). Partial/substring match. Example: "Amyris". This lists recorded transfers into the party (one row per transfer, at most 25), not the patents it owns, and finds nothing for a company with no recorded transfer. For "patents assigned to X" / "X's patents" / "patents owned by X", use the patent search tool's `applicant` filter instead.

assignor.description: Company or person who assigned rights AWAY in a recorded transfer (the inventor or prior owner). Partial/substring match. Example: "Musk"

patent_number.description: A granted US patent number, digits only. Example: "10000000".

application_number.description: A US application number, digits only or formatted. Example: "15000001", "15/000,001".

limit.description: Maximum assignment records to return (default 10, max 25). For an assignee/assignor search this also bounds the number of follow-up property lookups, so a higher limit costs more upstream calls.

_apiKey.description: Not used by this tool — USPTO Assignment Search is keyless. Present only for schema parity with the other tools in this pack.

instructions: @pipeworx/mcp-patents forwards to the Pipeworx gateway and lists only the patents pack's tools. Set PIPEWORX_META_TOOLS=1 to also list ask_pipeworx and the other gateway-wide tools.
